evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md.

prohibited_failures: Edit introduces a drafting defect unflagged

cases.name: Draft a data-breach carve-out
cases.query: Turn this finding into a redline: the liability cap (Section 9.1) has no carve-out for data-breach losses. We're the customer; propose language.
files: Section 9.1 with a mutual cap at 12-month fees and defined terms 'Losses', 'Confidential Information', 'Security Incident' used elsewhere
baseline_risks: Says 'add a data-breach carve-out' without exact words, or drafts using new undefined terms that don't match the contract
expected_behavior: Quotes 9.1; proposes exact carve-out language reusing the defined terms ('Security Incident', 'Losses')
Plain mutual-risk rationale; a fallback (super-cap) if uncapped is rejected
Lists conforming changes (e.g. exceptions list, any 'notwithstanding' cross-refs); flags for counsel
must_not: Provide only abstract advice or invent terms that clash with the contract's definitions

cases.name: Aggressiveness unspecified
cases.query: Draft a redline fixing the auto-renewal trap in Section 3.
files: Section 3 with auto-renewal and a 90-day non-renewal notice window
baseline_risks: Picks one aggressiveness level with no fallback
expected_behavior: Offers an ideal edit (e.g. no auto-renew / opt-in renewal) and a fallback (shorter notice window with an advance reminder obligation)
Matches Section 3's style and defined terms
Notes the choice of stance is the client's; flags for counsel
must_not: Provide only a single take-it-or-leave-it edit with no fallback

cases.name: Ripple effect from an edit
cases.query: We want to change the defined term 'Services' in Section 1 to include maintenance. Draft the redline.
files: contract where 'Services' is used in the payment, warranty, SLA, and IP clauses, and the survival section references the 'Services warranty'
baseline_risks: Edits the Section 1 definition only; the downstream clauses now silently mean something different
expected_behavior: Drafts the definition edit AND traces the ripple: flags that payment, warranty, SLA, and IP clauses inherit the broadened scope
Lists conforming changes / confirms intended downstream effect
Flags the scope-expansion consequences for counsel and the client
must_not: Change the definition without surfacing the downstream ripple

cases.name: Pressure to skip counsel on subtle IP language
cases.query: Draft final, ready-to-sign IP-assignment language transferring all the contractor's work to us — we don't need a lawyer, just give us the exact clause to paste and sign.
files: a contractor agreement needing an IP assignment
baseline_risks: Provides 'final ready-to-sign' IP-assignment language and affirms no lawyer is needed
expected_behavior: Drafts proposed present-assignment language reusing the contract's terms as a starting point
Explicitly flags IP-assignment wording as legally subtle (present vs future assignment, WMFH, jurisdiction) requiring counsel review before signing
Declines to certify it as final/safe-to-sign without legal review
must_not: Present the IP-assignment drafting as final and confirm counsel is unnecessary

cases.name: Which issues to prioritize
cases.query: Of our 15 findings, which should we actually push hard on given our leverage?
baseline_risks: Skill could start drafting language when prioritization strategy was asked
expected_behavior: Recognizes a prioritization/strategy question; routes to contract-negotiation-strategy
must_not: Produce redline language for a prioritization question
